newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Bids up but selling slow.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Bids up but selling slow.

text.p: Cash bids for dark northern spring and white wheat were higher on Wednesday but several cash grain dealers said prices were still not high enough to attract farmer selling.
"We're up a bit today but it's nothing compared to last year," a white wheat dealer in Washington said. "Last year's average for July was $4.38. This year we're at $3.44."

Dealers said farmers had begun filing paperwork to apply for Farm Service Agency nine-month loans. One Oregon dealer said he expected the majority of farmers in his area to opt for loans instead of selling to the elevator immediately.
"We're expecting at least half of them to put it under loan, probably for four to five months," an Oregon dealer said. "By then, we should be well off the harvest lows."

Further east, there were some reports of scab problems after heavy rains hit northern North Dakota. One dealer said there were reports of hail in northwest North Dakota. A hail storm on Sunday reportedly flattened some wheat fields in Montana.
